correctness.rationale: Exact graph definitions and quantifiers (all even n=2k with k>=4, plus the separately stated odd and n=6 cases) are explicit. Each selected vertex has a closed neighborhood of at most four; the overlap identity Omega=4|S|-e-2n excludes 00 for all claimed even lengths and odd lengths. A gap count forces exactly the A(r,j,s), L_s and R_s words and proves they dominate; a complete symbolic comparison derives every edge and exactly two twin double-brooms plus isolates. Direct exhaustive subset enumeration for n=5..12 and separate symbolic all-pair adjacency verification for k=4..26 both passed. Infinite coverage is from the algebraic word proof, not finite sampling.
residual_risks: Proof is handwritten case analysis, not independently peer reviewed; finite tests are noncertifying for the infinite family.

originality.rationale: Published foundational gamma-graph work introduces the same adjacent-exchange operation but inspected accessible material does not identify the present double-broom decomposition; other candidate papers use unrestricted token jumping, addition/deletion, or the middle graph of a ladder. The older bare number of minimum dominating sets is expressly not claimed new. All published-finding corpus searches and accessible own-claim history were compared on implication, not title alone. A missing full text of the 2011 founding paper and a 2024 product-focused paper is named as substantive residual priority risk, not classified as definitely noncovering.
residual_risks: The Fricke et al. 2011 paper is exactly the same reconfiguration model; its full text was not recovered. It might contain unindexed ladder examples.
Bhatt 2024 paper on Cartesian products of paths and cycles was only accessible as an abstract; an unrecognized equivalent or stronger result remains possible.
No claim that semantic search absence demonstrates mathematical uniqueness; inaccessible previous-week prior research claim files cannot be fully excluded.

value.rationale: The natural reconfiguration question asks whether minimum guards on a basic Cartesian grid can be moved without adding guards or losing coverage. A sharp entire-family decomposition into two mobile double-brooms and a linearly growing frozen stratum is a substantive graph invariant; exact component diameters, degrees and counts are not implied by the known domination number or minimum-set count. This determines feasible optimal transformations and exact obstructions.
residual_risks: No theorem for wider grids is implied or claimed.
